cards.explanation: The answer is that He comes to carry out His anger and rebuke. The verse says the LORD will come with fire, and His chariots are like a whirlwind. He comes "…to execute His anger with fury and His rebuke with flames of fire." (Isaiah 66:15) This is a heavy picture, friends, and the text doesn't soften it.

The answer is True. The verse says, "For by fire and by His sword, the LORD will execute judgment on all flesh, and many will be slain by the LORD." (Isaiah 66:16) Fire and sword, and it reaches all flesh. It's a serious line, friends, so I'll let it be serious.

The answer is True. The LORD declares that those who consecrate and purify themselves to enter the groves, following one in the center of those who eat the flesh of swine and vermin and rats, "…will perish together…" (Isaiah 66:17) All that preparing, and it's aimed at the wrong place. The text says they perish together.

The answer is every nation and language. The LORD says He is "…coming to gather all nations and tongues…" (Isaiah 66:18) Tongues just means languages, friends. So the guest list is wide open, and no language is left off it.
The answer is the LORD's glory. The LORD says all nations and tongues "…will come and see My glory." (Isaiah 66:18) His glory is the thing the verse says they will see, friends.

The answer is False. The verse describes "…the islands far away who have not heard of My fame or seen My glory." (Isaiah 66:19) They haven't heard it yet, friends. The same verse says the LORD will send survivors to the nations.
The word is proclaim. The LORD says, "So they will proclaim My glory among the nations." (Isaiah 66:19) To proclaim is to announce it out loud, friends. These survivors go out and speak it.

The answer is Jerusalem. The LORD says they'll be brought "…to My holy mountain Jerusalem…" (Isaiah 66:20) The verse lists horses, chariots, wagons, mules and camels. That's a whole parade, friends, all headed to one place.

The answer is bringing an offering in a clean vessel. The LORD says it's "just as the Israelites bring an offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD." (Isaiah 66:20) So the brothers are the gift, friends, and the LORD compares it to an offering brought in a clean vessel.

The answer is priests and Levites. The LORD says, "And I will select some of them as priests and Levites…" (Isaiah 66:21) Those are the two roles named, friends. And notice who does the selecting: the LORD says He will.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "For just as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, will endure before Me… so your descendants and your name will endure." (Isaiah 66:22) The promise is tied to something He makes, friends. So the name endures as long as the new heavens and new earth do.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "…all mankind will come to worship before Me…" (Isaiah 66:23) It happens from one New Moon to another and one Sabbath to another, friends. It's not only Israel.

The answer is the corpses of those who rebelled, and it's a heavy one. The LORD says, "As they go forth, they will see the corpses of the men who have rebelled against Me…" (Isaiah 66:24) I think this verse is meant to be taken seriously, friends. The text doesn't make it light, so I won't either.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "…their worm will never die, their fire will never be quenched, and they will be a horror to all mankind." (Isaiah 66:24) Never quenched means it isn't put out, friends. It's a heavy way to end the book, and I won't dress it up.
